projects.title: Unique Paths I (2D Grid Path Counting DP)
projects.description: Find total unique paths from top-left `(0,0)` to bottom-right `(M-1, N-1)` on an `M x N` grid moving only DOWN or RIGHT. Recurrence relation: `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]` with base cases `dp[i][0] = 1, dp[0][j] = 1`. Solved in `O(M * N)` time! In this project, you will build Unique Paths 2D Grid DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2D Grid Path Counting, Additive Subproblem Recurrences & Space Optimization to 1D Row Array
projects.exampleText: Find unique paths on 3x7 grid
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Unique Paths I (2D Grid DP) ---
Unique Paths on 3x7 grid = 28
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Base Boundaries**: Set `dp[i][0] = 1` and `dp[0][j] = 1`.
2. **Path Sum**: `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `unique_paths()`: Solves Unique Paths I using 2D Grid DP.

projects.title: Unique Paths II (2D Grid with Obstacles DP)
projects.description: Find unique paths on an `M x N` grid containing obstacles (`grid[i][j] == 1`). If a cell has an obstacle, set `dp[i][j] = 0` (no paths through obstacles). If starting cell `(0,0)` is an obstacle, return 0 in O(M * N) time! In this project, you will build Unique Paths II Obstacle Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Grid Obstacle Handling, Zero-Path State Resets & Boundary Obstacle Propagation
projects.exampleText: Compute unique paths avoiding grid obstacles
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Unique Paths II (2D Grid with Obstacles DP) ---
Unique Paths avoiding grid obstacles = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Obstacle Rule**: If `grid[i][j] == 1`, set `dp[i][j] = 0`.
2. **Path Accumulation**: `dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1]` for non-obstacle cells.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `unique_paths_obstacles_demo()`: Solves Unique Paths II with grid obstacles.

projects.title: Minimum Path Sum in 2D Grid
projects.description: Find path from `(0,0)` to `(M-1, N-1)` that MINIMIZES total sum of numbers along the path. Recurrence: `dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])` in `O(M * N)` time! In this project, you will build Minimum Path Sum 2D Grid Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Grid Sum Minimization, Dynamic Boundary Initialization & 2D Recurrence Transitions
projects.exampleText: Find minimum path sum on 3x3 grid
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Path Sum in 2D Grid ---
Minimum Path Sum = 7
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Boundary Precompute**: Accumulate first row and first column sums.
2. **Min Transition**: `dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_path_sum()`: Solves Minimum Path Sum in 2D Grid.

projects.title: Triangle Minimum Path Sum (Top-Down to Bottom-Up DP)
projects.description: Given a triangle array, find minimum path sum from top to bottom moving to adjacent numbers on row below. Solved in-place using Bottom-Up DP: `dp[row][col] += min(dp[row+1][col], dp[row+1][col+1])` in O(N^2) time and O(1) extra space! In this project, you will build Triangle Path DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Triangle In-Place Bottom-Up DP, Subtree Minimum Propagation & O(1) Extra Space
projects.exampleText: Compute triangle minimum path sum
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Triangle Minimum Path Sum (Bottom-Up DP) ---
Triangle Minimum Path Sum = 11
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bottom-Up Sweep**: Start at bottom-1 row and iterate up to apex.
2. **In-Place Recurrence**: `triangle[r][c] += min(triangle[r+1][c], triangle[r+1][c+1])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `triangle_min_path_demo()`: Solves Triangle Minimum Path Sum using Bottom-Up DP.

projects.title: 0-1 Knapsack Problem (Classic Item Selection DP)
projects.description: Given N items with weights `wt[i]` and values `val[i]`, find maximum value that fits in knapsack capacity W (each item taken AT MOST ONCE). 2D DP state `dp[i][w]` stores max value using first `i` items with capacity `w`: `dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], val[i-1] + dp[i-1][w - wt[i-1]])` in `O(N * W)` time! In this project, you will build 0-1 Knapsack Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 0-1 Knapsack DP Formulation, Item Selection Choice (Take vs Skip) & Capacity States
projects.exampleText: Find maximum value for capacity W=50 with 3 items
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 0-1 Knapsack Problem (Classic 2D DP) ---
Maximum Value = 220
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **2D DP Table**: `dp[i][w]` rows represent items `0..N`, columns represent capacity `0..W`.
2. **Take/Skip Choice**: `max(dp[i-1][w], val[i-1] + dp[i-1][w - wt[i-1]])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `knapsack_01()`: Solves classic 0-1 Knapsack Problem using 2D DP.

projects.title: 0-1 Knapsack Space Optimization (1D Reverse Array dp[w])
projects.description: Since `dp[i][w]` depends ONLY on previous row `dp[i-1]`, compress 2D table into a 1D array `dp[w]`. Crucial rule: iterate capacity `w` IN REVERSE (`W` down to `wt[i]`) to prevent using the same item multiple times in `O(W)` memory! In this project, you will build 1D Space Optimized 0-1 Knapsack in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 1D Knapsack Space Optimization, Reverse Loop Invariants & Memory Compression
projects.exampleText: Solve 0-1 Knapsack using 1D reverse array dp[w]
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 0-1 Knapsack 1D Space Optimization ---
Maximum Value = 220
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Reverse Capacity Loop**: Loop `w` from `W` down to `wt[i]`.
2. **1D Update**: `dp[w] = max(dp[w], val[i] + dp[w - wt[i]])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `knapsack_01_space_opt()`: Solves 0-1 Knapsack using 1D reverse array space optimization.

projects.title: Unbounded Knapsack Problem (Infinite Item Reuse DP)
projects.description: Given N items, each item can be selected AN UNLIMITED NUMBER OF TIMES. In 1D space optimization, iterate capacity `w` FORWARD (`wt[i]` up to `W`) to allow multiple inclusions of the same item in `O(N * W)` time! In this project, you will build Unbounded Knapsack Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Unbounded Knapsack Formulations, Forward Capacity Loop Iterations & Unlimited Item Reuse
projects.exampleText: Maximize value with infinite item reuse for capacity W=100
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Unbounded Knapsack Problem (Infinite Reuse DP) ---
Maximum Value with infinite item reuse = 300
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Forward Capacity Loop**: Loop `w` from `wt[i]` up to `W`.
2. **Multiple Inclusions**: Forward iteration allows updated values at `w - wt[i]` to be reused.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `unbounded_knapsack_demo()`: Solves Unbounded Knapsack with infinite item reuse.

projects.title: Target Sum (Assign + / - Signs to Array Elements)
projects.description: Given integer array `nums` and target, assign `+` or `-` to each element so that sum equals target. Mathematical reduction: partition `nums` into positive set P and negative set N: `sum(P) = (total_sum + target) / 2`. Converts to 0-1 Knapsack Subset Sum in O(N * Target) time! In this project, you will build Target Sum Knapsack Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Mathematical Sign Assignment Reduction, 0-1 Knapsack Target Halving & Subset Sums
projects.exampleText: Count sign assignment ways to reach target sum
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Target Sum (Knapsack Sign Assignment DP) ---
Total Ways to assign + / - signs to get target sum = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Subset Reduction**: `P_sum = (total_sum + target) / 2`.
2. **Knapsack DP**: Count subsets with sum equal to `P_sum`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `target_sum_knapsack_demo()`: Solves Target Sum using 0-1 Knapsack subset sum reduction.

projects.title: Ones and Zeroes (2D Capacity 3D State Knapsack DP)
projects.description: Given binary strings array, find maximum subset size such that total 0s `<= m` and total 1s `<= n`. Multi-dimensional Knapsack DP state `dp[i][j]` stores max subset for `i` zeros and `j` ones: `dp[i][j] = max(dp[i][j], 1 + dp[i - zeros][j - ones])`. In this project, you will build Multi-Capacity Knapsack Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Multi-Dimensional Knapsack DP, Dual Capacity Constraints & 2D Matrix DP Arrays
projects.exampleText: Find maximum binary string subset under 5 zeros and 3 ones constraints
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Ones and Zeroes (2D Capacity 3D State Knapsack DP) ---
Maximum Subset Size under 5 zeros and 3 ones constraints = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Dual Constraint**: 2 capacity limits (`m` zeros, `n` ones).
2. **2D Reverse Iteration**: Iterate `i` from `m` down to `zeros`, `j` from `n` down to `ones`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `ones_and_zeroes_demo()`: Solves Ones and Zeroes multi-capacity Knapsack DP.

projects.title: Maximal Square in 2D Binary Matrix
projects.description: Given an `R x C` binary matrix of '1's and '0's, find the area of the largest square containing only 1s. DP state `dp[i][j]` stores side length of max square with bottom-right corner at `(i,j)`: `dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1])` in `O(R * C)` time! In this project, you will build Maximal Square Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Maximal Square DP Recurrences, Bottom-Right Corner Anchoring & 3-Neighbor Minimums
projects.exampleText: Find area of largest 1s square in 2D matrix
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximal Square in 2D Binary Matrix ---
Maximal Square Area of 1s in Matrix = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **3-Neighbor Rule**: Square grows if top, left, and top-left neighbors are all valid square corners.
2. **Min Recurrence**: `dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `maximal_square_demo()`: Solves Maximal Square in 2D binary matrix using DP.

projects.title: Dungeon Game (Bottom-Right to Top-Left Health DP)
projects.description: A knight starts at top-left `(0,0)` and must reach princess at bottom-right `(M-1, N-1)` on a grid with health gains/losses. Find MINIMUM initial health required to stay alive (`health >= 1` at all times). Iterate BACKWARDS from bottom-right to top-left in O(M * N) time! In this project, you will build Dungeon Game Health DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Reverse Grid Traversal DP, Minimum Initial State Guarantees & Health Invariants
projects.exampleText: Calculate minimum initial health required for knight
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dungeon Game (Bottom-Right to Top-Left Health DP) ---
Minimum Initial Health Required = 7
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Backward Iteration**: Compute `dp[i][j]` from bottom-right `(M-1, N-1)`.
2. **Health Recurrence**: `needed = min(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j+1]) - dungeon[i][j]`; `dp[i][j] = max(1, needed)`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dungeon_game_demo()`: Solves Dungeon Game minimum initial health using reverse 2D DP.

projects.title: Minimum Falling Path Sum
projects.description: Given an `N x N` matrix, find minimum sum of falling path starting at any element in first row and ending at any element in last row. Allowed moves from `(r, c)` are `(r+1, c-1)`, `(r+1, c)`, `(r+1, c+1)`. Solved in `O(N^2)` time! In this project, you will build Minimum Falling Path Sum Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Falling Path 3-Neighbor Recurrences, Top-to-Bottom Grid DP & Dynamic Row Sweeps
projects.exampleText: Find minimum falling path sum on NxN grid
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Falling Path Sum ---
Minimum Falling Path Sum = 13
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **3-Direction Move**: From `(r-1, c-1)`, `(r-1, c)`, `(r-1, c+1)`.
2. **Min Recurrence**: `dp[r][c] = matrix[r][c] + min(dp[r-1][c-1], dp[r-1][c], dp[r-1][c+1])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_falling_path_demo()`: Solves Minimum Falling Path Sum using 2D DP.

projects.title: Cherry Pickup I (2-Person Simultaneous Grid Path DP)
projects.description: Find max cherries collected going `(0,0) -> (N-1,N-1)` and returning `(N-1,N-1) -> (0,0)`. Model as TWO people moving simultaneously from `(0,0)` to `(N-1,N-1)`. State `dp[step][r1][r2]` tracks step count `r1 + c1 == r2 + c2`, reducing 4D state to 3D in O(N^3) time! In this project, you will build Cherry Pickup 3D DP Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Simultaneous 2-Path Grid DP, State Dimension Reduction (4D to 3D) & Shared Cell Adjustments
projects.exampleText: Collect maximum cherries via simultaneous 2-path DP
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Cherry Pickup I (2-Person Simultaneous Grid DP) ---
Maximum Cherries Collected = 5
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Step Invariant**: `c1 = step - r1`, `c2 = step - r2`.
2. **Shared Cell Deduplication**: If `r1 == r2` and `c1 == c2`, add cherry ONCE.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cherry_pickup_demo()`: Solves Cherry Pickup I using 3D State DP.

projects.title: Bounded Knapsack Problem (Multiplicity Item Constraints)
projects.description: Given N items with weights, values, and quantities `count[i]`, find max value for capacity W. Decompose item counts into Binary Powers of 2 (`1, 2, 4, 8...`) to convert Bounded Knapsack to 0-1 Knapsack in `O(W * sum(log count[i]))` time! In this project, you will build Bounded Knapsack Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bounded Knapsack Multiplicities, Binary Power Item Decompositions & 0-1 Knapsack Conversion
projects.exampleText: Solve Bounded Knapsack with binary item counts decomposition
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bounded Knapsack Problem (Binary Decomposed DP) ---
Maximum Value with bounded item counts = 180
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Binary Decomposition**: Decompose `count[i]` into power of 2 bundles (`1, 2, 4, remaining`).
2. **0-1 Knapsack Transformation**: Run standard 0-1 Knapsack on generated item bundles.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bounded_knapsack_demo()`: Solves Bounded Knapsack via binary item decomposition.

projects.title: Fractional Knapsack Greedy vs 0-1 Dynamic Programming Comparison
projects.description: Compare Fractional Knapsack (items can be broken, solved via Greedy Value/Weight ratio sorting in O(N log N)) vs 0-1 Knapsack (items cannot be broken, solved via DP in O(N * W)). Demonstrate why Greedy FAILS on 0-1 Knapsack! In this project, you will build Knapsack Comparison Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Greedy vs Dynamic Programming Invariants, Item Divisibility & Counter-Example Proofs
projects.exampleText: Compare Fractional Knapsack (Greedy) vs 0-1 Knapsack (DP)
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Fractional Knapsack (Greedy) vs 0-1 Knapsack (DP) ---
Fractional Knapsack Max Value: 240.0
0-1 Knapsack Max Value: 220
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Fractional Greedy**: Sort by `val/wt`; take partial fractions of items.
2. **0-1 DP**: Full item choices only; DP avoids greedy local optimal traps.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `knapsack_comparison_demo()`: Benchmarks Fractional Knapsack vs 0-1 Knapsack.

projects.title: Last Stone Weight II (Knapsack Subset Sum Reduction)
projects.description: Smash stones together pair by pair (weights `x` and `y` become `y - x`). Find minimum possible weight of last remaining stone. Problem reduces to partitioning stones into two subsets with minimum weight difference! Find max subset sum `<= total_sum / 2` using 0-1 Knapsack DP in O(N * Sum) time. In this project, you will build Last Stone Weight II Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Stone Smashing Reductions, Minimum Subset Difference & 0-1 Knapsack Partitioning
projects.exampleText: Find minimum possible weight of last remaining stone
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Last Stone Weight II (Subset Sum Knapsack DP) ---
Minimum possible weight of last remaining stone = 1
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Subset Partition**: `target = total_sum / 2`.
2. **Min Difference**: `MinWeight = total_sum - 2 * max_subset_sum`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `last_stone_weight_ii_demo()`: Solves Last Stone Weight II using 0-1 Knapsack DP.

projects.title: Out of Boundary Paths (3D Grid State DP)
projects.description: Given `M x N` grid, ball starting at `(startRow, startColumn)`, find total paths to move ball out of grid boundary within AT MOST `maxMove` steps. 3D DP state `dp[move][r][c]` tracks step counts in O(maxMove * M * N) time! In this project, you will build Out of Boundary Paths Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 3D Grid DP States `(move, r, c)`, Boundary Step Counting & Modulo Path Additions
projects.exampleText: Find total out of boundary paths within maxMove=2
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Out of Boundary Paths (3D Grid State DP) ---
Total Out of Boundary Paths within maxMove=2 = 6
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Boundary Check**: If neighbor `(r', c')` is outside grid, add current state paths to result.
2. **4-Neighbor Transition**: Accumulate paths across `move - 1` step states.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `out_of_boundary_paths_demo()`: Solves Out of Boundary Paths using 3D Grid State DP.

projects.title: Minimum Swaps To Make Sequences Increasing
projects.description: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, find minimum swaps at index `i` (swapping `nums1[i]` and `nums2[i]`) to make both sequences strictly increasing. Maintain 2 DP states: `keep[i]` and `swap[i]` in O(N) time! In this project, you will build Min Swaps Sequences Increasing Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Sequence Swap DP, 2-State Invariants (Keep vs Swap) & State Dependent Transitions
projects.exampleText: Calculate minimum swaps to make sequences strictly increasing
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Swaps To Make Sequences Increasing ---
Minimum swaps required = 1
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Keep State**: `keep[i]` tracks min swaps without swapping index `i`.
2. **Swap State**: `swap[i]` tracks min swaps with swapping index `i`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_swaps_increasing_demo()`: Solves Minimum Swaps To Make Sequences Increasing.

projects.title: Profitable Schemes (2-Constraint Group Knapsack DP)
projects.description: Given `G` group members, `minProfit` target, and crime schemes with member requirements `group[i]` and profits `profit[i]`, find total profitable schemes using at most G members. 3D Knapsack DP state `dp[members][profit]` in `O(N * G * minProfit)` time! In this project, you will build Profitable Schemes Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Group Knapsack Constraints, Dual Capacity DP (Members & Profit) & Scheme Combinations
projects.exampleText: Calculate total profitable crime schemes under member constraints
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Profitable Schemes (2-Constraint Group Knapsack DP) ---
Total Profitable Schemes = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Profit Cap**: Cap profit state at `minProfit` using `min(minProfit, p + profit[i])`.
2. **2D Reverse Iteration**: Iterate members `G` down to `group[i]`, profit `minProfit` down to 0.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `profitable_schemes_demo()`: Solves Profitable Schemes using multi-constraint Knapsack DP.

projects.title: Shortest Path in 2D Grid with Obstacle Elimination (Grid BFS + DP State)
projects.description: Find shortest path from `(0,0)` to `(R-1, C-1)` on a grid with obstacles, given you can eliminate AT MOST K obstacles. 3D BFS State `(r, c, k_rem)` tracks remaining obstacle elimation quota in `O(R * C * K)` time! In this project, you will build Grid Obstacle Elimination BFS in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Grid BFS with State Quotas, Obstacle Elimination Transitions & Shortest Path Guarantees
projects.exampleText: Find shortest grid path with K=1 obstacle eliminations
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Shortest Path in Grid with Obstacle Elimination ---
Shortest path length with K=1 obstacle eliminations = 6
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **3D Visited Matrix**: Track `visited[r][c][k_rem]`.
2. **Obstacle Pass**: Decrement `k_rem - 1` when stepping onto obstacle cell.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `obstacle_elimination_grid_demo()`: Solves Shortest Path in Grid with Obstacle Elimination.

projects.title: Monotone Queue DP Optimization (Sliding Window Maximum Knapsack DP) in O(N W)
projects.description: Optimize Bounded Knapsack DP transitions from `O(N * W * K)` down to `O(N * W)` using a Monotone Queue (Sliding Window Maximum Deque) over remainder congruence classes modulo `wt[i]`! In this project, you will build Monotone Queue Knapsack Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Monotone Queue DP Optimizations, Congruence Class Remainder Deques & Sliding Window Maximums
projects.exampleText: Optimize Bounded Knapsack from O(N W K) to O(N W) via Monotone Deque
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Monotone Queue DP Optimization (Sliding Window Maximum Knapsack) ---
Optimized Bounded Knapsack DP transition from O(N * W * K) to O(N * W) using Monotone Deque.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Congruence Classes**: Group capacity states by `w % wt[i]`.
2. **Monotone Deque**: Maintain monotonic decreasing sliding window deque over capacity states.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `monotone_queue_knapsack_demo()`: Solves Monotone Queue DP optimization for Bounded Knapsack.

projects.title: Bitset Accelerated Knapsack Subset Sum Engine (64x Speedup)
projects.description: Accelerate 0-1 Knapsack Subset Sum queries over 100,000 items using 64-bit integer bitset shifts `dp |= (dp << weight)` in C, evaluating 64 capacity states in 1 CPU clock instruction (64x hardware speedup)! In this project, you will build Bitset Knapsack Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 64-Bit Word Bitset Shifts (`dp << weight`), Bitwise Subset Sum Acceleration & Hardware Parallelism
projects.exampleText: Execute bitset shift `dp |= (dp << num)` for 64x hardware speedup
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bitset Accelerated Knapsack Subset Sum Engine ---
Executed bitset shift `dp |= (dp << num)` for 64x hardware speedup on 100,000 items.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bitset Word Shift**: Shift 64-bit unsigned long bitset array by `weight`.
2. **Bitwise OR Union**: `dp[w] |= (dp[w - shift] << offset)` updates 64 states simultaneously.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bitset_knapsack_demo()`: Implements Bitset Accelerated Knapsack Subset Sum Engine.

projects.title: 2D Grid Dynamic Programming State Compression (1D Rolling Arrays)
projects.description: Compress 2D Grid DP matrices `dp[R][C]` down to 1D Rolling Arrays `dp[C]` (or 2-row rolling buffers `dp[2][C]`), reducing RAM memory consumption from `O(R * C)` down to `O(C)`! In this project, you will build 2D Grid DP Memory Compressor in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Rolling Array Memory Compression, Row Parity Modulo `row % 2` & Memory Footprint Reductions
projects.exampleText: Compress 2D Grid DP memory from O(R*C) to 1D rolling array O(C)
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 2D Grid Dynamic Programming State Compression ---
Compressed 2D Grid DP memory from O(R * C) down to 1D Rolling Array O(C) memory.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Rolling Row Index**: Access row using `curr = row % 2` and `prev = (row - 1) % 2`.
2. **Memory Reduction**: Reduces memory from Megabytes to Kilobytes for huge grids.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `grid_dp_compression_demo()`: Solves 2D Grid DP state memory compression.

projects.title: Parallel SIMD Vectorized 2D Grid DP Matrix Kernel
projects.description: High-speed scientific computing kernels accelerate 2D Grid DP matrix updates using 256-bit AVX2 SIMD vector instructions, evaluating 8 grid column DP cells concurrently in 1 CPU instruction pass! In this project, you will build SIMD 2D Grid DP Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: SIMD AVX2 2D Grid DP Vectorization, Parallel Matrix Cell Recurrences & Hardware Vector Pass

projects.codeExplanation: 1. `simd_2d_grid_dp_demo()`: Simulates SIMD vectorized 2D Grid DP matrix kernel.

projects.title: High-Throughput Memory-Mapped Real-Time Grid Route Optimizer
projects.description: Industrial autonomous robotics engines evaluate 5,000,000 streaming 2D grid DP path route queries per second over memory-mapped shared memory buffers (`mmap`) with zero system-call overhead. In this project, you will build Real-Time Grid Route Optimizer in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Memory-Mapped Grid DP Buffers, 5M Stream Route Optimizations & Robotics Grid Navigation

2. **Real-Time Path Optimization**: Execute zero-copy 2D Grid DP route updates directly from RAM offsets.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stream_grid_route_dp_demo()`: Simulates high-throughput memory-mapped real-time grid route optimizer.
